reconstructed_theorem: For every complete real inner product space E and every continuous real-linear endomorphism H:E→E satisfying ⟨Hu,v⟩=⟨u,Hv⟩ for all u,v∈E, define f:E→ℝ by f(z)=⟨z,Hz⟩/2. Then for every real h, every natural number N (including zero), and every x∈E, the N-fold iterate starting at x of T(z)=z−h∇f(z) equals (I−hH)^N x. The power of an endomorphism means repeated composition, and the zeroth iterate and zeroth endomorphism power are both the identity. The gradient is taken in the real inner product structure; the displayed quadratic is differentiable under these assumptions. There are no positivity, spectral, finite-dimensionality, or step-size restrictions. In particular h=0 and N=0 are included, and no convergence or contraction conclusion is asserted.
observations: The exact quadratic normalization is 1/2. All h∈ℝ are permitted, and H need only be bounded linear and symmetric on the complete real inner product space.

reconstructed_theorem: For every complete real inner product space E, every continuous real-linear endomorphism H:E→E satisfying ⟨Hu,v⟩=⟨u,Hv⟩ for all u,v∈E, every μ∈ℝ and every x∈E with Hx=μx, define f(y)=⟨y,Hy⟩/2. For every h∈ℝ and N∈ℕ, put z=T^[N](x), where T(y)=y−h∇f(y). Then simultaneously z=(1−hμ)^N x, ‖z‖=|1−hμ|^N‖x‖, and f(z)=(1−hμ)^(2N)f(x). Here iteration at N=0 is the identity and every zeroth power, including 0^0, is 1. Neither x≠0 nor μ>0 nor h>0 is assumed, and there is no step-size restriction. Thus zero starting vectors, zero step size, zero μ, and 1−hμ=0 are included. In the last case z=0 for N≥1, whereas N=0 still gives z=x. These are exact identities and assert no contraction, decay rate, convergence, or sign of f.
observations: The condition Hx=μx includes x=0 for every real μ; calling x an eigenvector would impose an additional nonzero hypothesis absent from this statement. The function-value multiplier has exponent 2N, while the norm multiplier is the Nth power of an absolute value.
